episode_title: He Handed Over 13 Years of Work for $100K w/ Alan Underwood

real_qa.q: How did Alan Underwood grow his car dealership to $60 million in revenue before selling it in 2020?
real_qa.r: By 2020, Underwood had built the dealership to two locations with about 30 employees, over 30,000 Facebook followers, and over $16 million in annual sales. He grew the business a million dollars year over year for 13 consecutive years after starting in May 2007, though he ultimately sold it after experiencing serious personal losses that affected his ability to operate.

real_qa.q: Why did Alan Underwood sell his $60 million car dealership for only $100,000?
real_qa.r: Underwood sold the business for approximately $100,000 to a friend after suffering major personal losses—his mother-in-law died of cancer in 2018, his father-in-law in 2019, and his father had a massive stroke in 2020. These losses led to depression and a collapse in his self-worth, causing him to undervalue the business he had built and simply want to exit quickly without contracts or formal negotiation.

real_qa.q: What was Alan Underwood's first Angel Flight West mission and why did he start flying for the charity?
real_qa.r: Underwood's first flight was for an 18-year-old named Bradley diagnosed with Hodgkin's lymphoma who needed treatment at a children's hospital five hours away. Bradley's mother had been driving three times a week (over 30 hours weekly), but Underwood's one-and-a-half hour flight each way was free to the family. After obtaining his pilot's license and seeking ways to help others through flying, Underwood discovered Angel Flight West and joined the organization.
real_qa.requete: Angel Flight West Bradley Hodgkin's lymphoma mission

real_qa.q: How many volunteers and missions does Angel Flight West operate annually across Western U.S. states?
real_qa.r: Angel Flight West has approximately 2,000 volunteer pilots across 13 Western states and completes 4,000 to 5,000 missions every year, providing non-emergency medical flights to people in need at no cost to the families.

real_qa.q: What key steps did Alan Underwood take to rebuild his life after selling his car dealership?
real_qa.r: Underwood's first critical step was choosing not to end his life when he was in crisis. He then got clear on his identity outside of business success, spent time in prayer and meditation to forgive himself, joined a paid mastermind group connecting him with 300-400 like-minded entrepreneurs, and hired a business coach who helped him rebuild his mindset and belief in himself rather than just business strategy.
real_qa.requete: Alan Underwood rebuild after business failure mastermind coach

guest.bio_context: Alan Underwood started a car dealership in May 2007 just before the financial market crash, borrowing against his house to fund the venture. Over 13 years, he grew it into a $60 million business with two locations, 30 employees, and over 30,000 Facebook followers generating $16 million in annual sales. After experiencing severe personal losses including the deaths of his mother-in-law, father-in-law, and father between 2018 and 2020, he sold the business for $100,000and later discovered Angel Flight West, eventually leading the Arizona chapter of this non-emergency medical flight charity serving 13 Western U.S. states.
